title: Reduce rebuild overhead by caching dependency graph and immutable module layers
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
Our monorepo CI spends ~45–70% of execution time reinstalling dependencies and re-executing unchanged build steps across jobs that run the same package sets. This increases developer feedback loops and consumes CI minutes.

Goal:
Introduce a dependency-graph level cache and immutable node_modules/docker layer strategy to avoid re-resolving and re-installing unchanged packages across builds and to enable fast incremental rebuilds for both PRs and trunk CI. This should reduce cold-build time for typical JS/TS change sets by ~40–60% and cut CI minutes for our shared test matrix.

Proposal summary:
1) Add a deterministic dependency graph hash (hash of lockfile + selected package.json files + resolved toolchain version) used as cache key.
2) Persist a prebuilt node_modules artifact in our remote cache and/or as a tagged Docker layer shared by jobs that have the same graph hash.
3) Leverage BuildKit cache-from/cache-to and layered Docker manifests to publish immutable module layers to our registry.
4) Add a CI step that computes the graph hash early and restores the corresponding layer/artifact; fallback to an install if not available and then publish the produced layer.
5) Enable selective invalidation: When only workspace-local source changes occur, reuse module layers and skip install entirely.
6) Update lint/toolchain containers to pin versions (ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript) and reuse the same layer strategy for lint runner images to avoid repeated container bootstraps.

Technical approach & details:
- Hash inputs: package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml (if present), workspace package.json files listed by the build target, .nvmrc (node version), .yarnrc or .npmrc, and any .npmrc authless registries.
- Artifact format: tarball of node_modules produced by a deterministic installer run (pnpm --frozen-lockfile or npm ci) plus a small metadata file with the lock hash and Node version. The tarball is stored in our remote cache and also used to create a Docker layer with a stable tag (ci-modules/<graph-hash>).
- CI integration: Modify existing build job templates in .github/workflows/build.yml and our internal GitHub Actions composite actions to run pre-cache-restore step. Use docker buildx build --cache-from=type=registry,ref=$REGISTRY/ci-modules:$GRAPH_HASH --cache-to=type=registry,mode=max,ref=$REGISTRY/ci-modules:$GRAPH_HASH to store layer. For non-dockerized jobs, add a cache restore from our blobstore by downloading and extracting the tarball.
- Lint/toolchain images: Build new lint-runner base images that already contain ESLint/Prettier/TypeScript pinned and cached in a separate layer; publish with tags that include toolchain versions so jobs can pull exact images.
- Rollout strategy: Pilot with one high-traffic repo (web-frontend) for 2 weeks, run canary builds on main and PRs, measure cache hit rate and CI time reduction, then expand to services team.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cold build time for web-frontend trunk job reduced by >=40% on average with cache hits documented.
- Cache hit rate >= 70% for PRs that only change source files and not package manifests across pilot repos.
- Published module layers are immutable and referenced by job logs (cache key visible in CI artifacts).
- Migration guide added to internal docs describing how to opt-in/out and how keys are computed.
- No change in test results or lint failures attributable to the new caching approach during pilot.

Risks & mitigations:
- Stale or corrupted node_modules artifacts: include metadata checksum and validation step; fallback to fresh install on mismatch.
- Secret registry auth in .npmrc: ensure cache keys strip auth tokens and CI restore uses ephemeral auth tokens injected at runtime.
- Cross-platform differences (linux musl vs glibc): produce artifacts per target platform and record platform in metadata.
- Cache pollution due to inconsistent lockfiles: enforce frozen-lockfile in install step and fail installs that would change lockfile.

Migrations & follow-ups:
- After pilot, expand to backend services and language runtimes (python/pip wheels caching) as a follow-up ticket.
- Investigate buildx remote cache pruning schedule and storage cost accounting.

Attachments / references:
- Proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CI/Dep+Graph+Cache+Proposal
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-frontend/pull/1224
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-builds/build-time-comparison
